signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/JPY trades at 110.69 as the G10 Currency Strength Scorecard prints an extreme 1.602% spread between AUD and JPY over the trailing week. AUD leads the G10 complex with an average gain of +0.959% across 4 pairs, whereas JPY lags at −0.644% across 7 pairs. The move is fundamentally underpinned by rate policy, where the RBA at 4.60% against the BoJ at 1.25% yields a 335bp carry advantage favoring the Australian dollar, reflected in an overnight AONIA-TONA spread of +337bp. Despite broad risk headlines around Middle East shipping corridors, VIX at 18.4 signals normal volatility, keeping carry-seeking flows insulated from safe-haven demand. Trade bias: Long AUD/JPY, carried by yield advantage while cross-asset volatility remains contained. Catalyst: Japan Adjusted Trade Balance release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: VIX surges above 25, prompting an abrupt liquidation of crowded JPY-funded carry trades.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Intervention Ceiling
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 158.55, trading above its SMA20 of 157.97 and SMA50 of 157.70, while holding directly beneath the SMA200 at 158.56. The Fed at 4.00% versus BoJ at 1.25% provides a +275bp policy rate cushion (+265bp on the SOFR-TONA CIP basis), which continues to anchor spot. However, options desks are actively hedging a reversal, as 1M ATM implied volatility of 7.7% trades 2.1 percentage points over HV30 of 5.6%, driving an elevated volatility risk premium alongside a sharp 25-delta risk reversal put skew of −1.97. Geopolitical warnings concerning the Strait of Hormuz reinforce tension near the psychological boundary, where 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention warnings. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported but capped below 160.00. Catalyst: BoJ policy meeting on 30 Oct. Risk: Spot sustains a break above 160.00, escalating imminent physical intervention risk from Japanese authorities.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Volatility Hedging
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1216, positioned below its SMA20 of 1.1274, SMA50 of 1.1465, and SMA200 of 1.1585 in a structural downtrend. CFTC data reveals leveraged funds hold a net short position of −92,833 contracts, placing speculative euro exposure at the 4th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of −1.78. Meanwhile, 1M implied volatility trades at 6.6% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.1%, generating a notable +2.5% volatility risk premium as traders pay up for tail coverage. With the Fed at 4.00% and the ECB at 2.65%, the 135bp rate spread (+144bp SOFR vs €STR) continues to favor the greenback, limiting recovery scope. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, supported by monetary divergence though vulnerable to short covering. Catalyst: UK and German CPI releases at 06:00 UTC. Risk: A daily close above the SMA20 at 1.1274 forces rapid covering of stretched institutional short positions.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Policy Divergence vs Retail Sentiment
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4104, holding below its 20-day moving average of 1.4192 while remaining comfortably above the SMA50 at 1.4000 and SMA200 at 1.3877. The Fed at 4.00% versus BoC at 2.25% delivers a +175bp policy advantage to the US dollar (+162bp on the SOFR-CORRA carry differential), reinforced by a US 2Y yield running 138bp above Canadian counterparts. leveraged funds maintain a heavy net short in CAD of −89,659 contracts (15th percentile of its 52-week distribution, z-score −1.32), whereas retail sentiment leans heavily contrarian with 74% of community traders positioned short USD/CAD. With Canadian headline CPI moderating to 3.1% year-on-year, the rate differential provides firm fundamental backing against retail fading. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, supported by a 175bp policy rate premium. Catalyst: BoC rate decision on 28 Oct. Risk: BoC delivers a surprise 25bp rate hike, compressing the bilateral yield advantage.
